answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake and prove useful work, so fake agents cost real capital instead of being free. Reputation then gathers slowly like water in an oasis: earned over time, hard to fake at scale. A light zephyr of random peer audits keeps the cost honest, and any agent caught duplicating work loses its stake. All attestations sit on a crystal-clear public ledger, so one operator spinning up a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand stakes and survive a thousand audits, turning a cheap flood into an expensive trickle.
